newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate spikes higher on weak peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate spikes higher on weak peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were up 1.55 percent at 20.75 percent in early trade on Tuesday in response to early weakness in the peso, dealers said.
"It's a reaction to the peso which had been very strong, a reflex action by dealers who were not sure the currency could stay where it was," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were meanwhile trading 2.7 centavos weaker at 7.8830/7.8860 per dollar.
Traders said secondary rates were also under upside pressure from surplus paper on the market as a result of Banco de Mxico operations to drain liquidity.
In April, the central bank began draining liquidity by assigning medium-term direct sales of paper and repos, rather than short-term cash deposit auctions as it had done previously.
Some 23.5 billion pesos of paper sold so far this month by the central bank as part of those operations has yet to come due.
Dealers said a sign of excess paper was that the spread between overnight government and bank rates had narrowed to zero.
Overnight rates on bank paper were meanwhile trading at 20.50 percent, or 140 basis points up from Monday's close.
Liquidity of 740 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
Dealers said the early rise in secondary rates had led them to predict gains at tonight's Cetes auction, as opposed to the cuts they expected on Monday.
